answer: When I think about someone with a lot on their plate, one person immediately stands out. The person who comes to mind is my mother, who somehow manages to juggle an enormous number of duties without ever seeming [[overwhelmed]]. Besides running the entire household, she helps look after my elderly grandparents in our ancestral village, which means travelling back and forth quite often, and she still finds time to help neighbours during any crisis. On top of that, she manages the household budget and keeps a close eye on my younger sister's studies. As for how she handles it all, what amazes me is how [[methodical]] she is; she plans her days carefully so nothing important slips through the cracks. She is usually up before everyone else, and by the time we sit down to breakfast half her list is already done. I have often seen her handle a sick relative, a household emergency and a family gathering all in the same week, yet she rarely complains. She has this quiet [[resilience]] that I deeply admire, and she genuinely believes that looking after others is a privilege rather than a burden. Whenever I feel stretched by my own comparatively minor workload, I think of her and feel slightly embarrassed. She has taught me that carrying responsibility gracefully is a skill in itself. Honestly, I consider her the most [[dependable]] person I know, and the whole family leans on her more than we probably realise. I really should tell her that more often.

followUps.q: Do you help your mother with her responsibilities?
followUps.answer: I try to, although not as much as I should. I do the shopping at the weekend and sometimes go with her to the village, but she still [[shoulders]] most of the work herself.

followUps.q: Do you think you will have more responsibilities in the future?
followUps.answer: Almost certainly. As my parents get older, I expect to take on more at home, and my career will bring its own pressures. I just hope I can cope with them as calmly as she does.

note: Placed grandparents in the ancestral village (persona), added budget and sister's studies as duties, a morning-routine detail and a reflective close.
